tytul: Whole or halved tomatoes packed in tomato juice (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for whole or halved tomatoes packed in tomato juice, with added acid, processed in a boiling-water bath.

akapity: According to an FDA list, tomatoes have an approximate pH of 4.30–4.90, and the value varies widely with variety and conditions.
Sugar may be added to balance the acidic taste, but the acid must not be left out.
Wash the tomatoes, dip them in boiling water for 30–60 seconds or until the skins split, then dip them in cold water.
Slip off the skins, remove the cores and leave the tomatoes whole or cut them in half.
Add the bottled lemon juice or citric acid to the jars, and if you like, 1 teaspoon of salt per quart jar.
Add 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid per quart jar (about 0.95 l) of tomatoes.
For pint jars, use 1 tablespoon of bottled lemon juice or 1/4 teaspoon of citric acid.
JarAtlas rule for metric jars: to a jar larger than a pint, of up to 946 ml (for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l), add acid as for a quart: 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid.
Raw pack: heat tomato juice in a saucepan and fill the jars with raw tomatoes, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Cover the tomatoes in the jars with hot tomato juice, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Hot pack: put the tomatoes in a large saucepan, add enough tomato juice to cover them completely and boil gently for 5 minutes.
Fill the jars with hot tomatoes, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace, and add hot tomato juice to cover them, again leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm).
For both packs, put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m), for hot or raw pack, process pint and quart jars in a boiling-water bath for 85 minutes.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints and quarts for 90 minutes.
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints and quarts for 95 minutes.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints and quarts for 100 minutes.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): this recipe has the same time for pints and quarts, so a jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, gets that time.
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so use smaller jars.
